"The journey of a thousand miles begins with one step."
- Loa Tzu

- Albert Camus

"It is not wisdom but Authority that makes a law."

answer:
1. “What does not kill me makes me stronger.”  
   — **Friedrich Nietzsche**, *Twilight of the Idols*

2. “One must still have chaos in oneself to be able to give birth to a dancing star.”  
   — **Friedrich Nietzsche**, *Thus Spoke Zarathustra*

3. “One must imagine Sisyphus happy.”  
   — **Albert Camus**, *The Myth of Sisyphus*

4. “I rebel—therefore we exist.”  
   — **Albert Camus**, *The Rebel*

5. “Man is condemned to be free.”  
   — **Jean-Paul Sartre**, *Existentialism Is a Humanism*

6. “Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom.”  
   — **Søren Kierkegaard**, *The Concept of Anxiety*

7. “Life swings like a pendulum to and fro between pain and boredom, and these two are in fact its ultimate constituents.”  
   — **Arthur Schopenhauer**, *The World as Will and Representation*

8. “The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.”  
   — **Marcus Aurelius**, *Meditations*, 5.20

9. “Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.”  
   — **Marcus Aurelius**, *Meditations*, 10.16

10. “Some things are in our control and others not.”  
    — **Epictetus**, *Enchiridion*, 1

11. “Don't demand that things happen as you wish, but wish that they happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.”  
    — **Epictetus**, *Enchiridion*, 8

12. “We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.”  
    — **Seneca**, *Letters to Lucilius*, 13

13. “It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.”  
    — **Seneca**, *On the Shortness of Life*

14. “The unexamined life is not worth living.”  
    — **Socrates**, in Plato’s *Apology*, 38a

15. “The heaviest penalty for declining to rule is to be ruled by someone inferior to yourself.”  
    — **Plato**, *Republic*, 347c

16. “He who overcomes others is strong; he who overcomes himself is mighty.”  
    — **Lao Tzu**, *Tao Te Ching*, 33

17. “To see what is right and not to do it is want of courage.”  
    — **Confucius**, *Analects*, 2.24

18. “A road is made by people walking on it.”  
    — **Zhuangzi**, *Zhuangzi*, chapter 2

19. “Purity and impurity depend on oneself; no one can purify another.”  
    — **The Buddha**, *Dhammapada*, 165

20. “Man is born free; and everywhere he is in chains.”  
    — **Jean-Jacques Rousseau**, *The Social Contract*

21. “Covenants, without the sword, are but words, and of no strength to secure a man at all.”  
    — **Thomas Hobbes**, *Leviathan*, chapter 17

22. “It is much safer to be feared than loved, when, of the two, either must be dispensed with.”  
    — **Niccolò Machiavelli**, *The Prince*, chapter 17

23. “Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign.”  
    — **John Stuart Mill**, *On Liberty*

24. “Have courage to use your own understanding!”  
    — **Immanuel Kant**, *An Answer to the Question: What Is Enlightenment?*

25. “Peace is not mere absence of war, but is a virtue that springs from force of character.”  
    — **Baruch Spinoza**, *Political Treatise*, 5.4

26. “The greatest thing in the world is to know how to belong to oneself.”  
    — **Michel de Montaigne**, *Essays*, “Of Solitude”

27. “To will oneself free is also to will others free.”  
    — **Simone de Beauvoir**, *The Ethics of Ambiguity*

28. “The good life is one inspired by love and guided by knowledge.”  
    — **Bertrand Russell**, *What I Believe*

29. “Rather than love, than money, than fame, give me truth.”  
    — **Henry David Thoreau**, *Walden*

30. “The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.”  
    — **Ludwig Wittgenstein**, *Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus*, 5.6
